source: Hand-written sample review of a sample pull request. Re-record a real one with `npm run record-fixture -- <pull request URL>`.

pr.title: Add search and pagination to the people table
pr.author: sample-author
pr.body: Adds a search box and Previous / Next pagination to the people table. The API now takes a query and a page and returns the total count.

findings.title: Search query is not URL encoded
findings.explanation: `query` comes straight from the search box. A value such as `R&D` or `a+b` changes the meaning of the query string, so the API receives `q=R` and an extra `D` parameter. Build the query with `URLSearchParams` so every value is encoded.
findings.suggestion: const response = await fetch(`/api/users?${new URLSearchParams({ q: query, page: String(page) })}`);

findings.title: Typing in the search box never refetches
findings.explanation: The effect reads `query` but only lists `page` as a dependency, so changing the search text does nothing until the page changes. Add `query` to the dependency list. You will probably also want to reset `page` to 0 when the query changes, otherwise a search from page 5 can land on an empty page.

findings.title: Out of order responses can overwrite newer results
findings.explanation: Each keystroke will start a request once `query` is a dependency. If an older request resolves after a newer one, the table shows results for the old query. There is also no `catch`, so a failed request becomes an unhandled rejection and the table silently keeps stale data. Ignore stale responses with an `ignore` flag or an `AbortController` in the effect cleanup, and show an error state on failure.

findings.title: Search input has no accessible name
findings.explanation: A placeholder is not a label: screen readers may not announce it, and it disappears as soon as the user types. Add a visible `<label>` or at least an `aria-label`.
findings.suggestion: <input aria-label="Search people" placeholder="Search people" value={query} onChange={(event) => setQuery(event.target.value)} />

findings.title: Clickable div cannot be reached with the keyboard
findings.explanation: The name is clickable but it is a `div`, so it is not focusable, has no role and does not respond to Enter or Space. Keyboard and screen reader users cannot select a person. Use a `button` (styled as a link if needed).

findings.title: Next stays enabled on the last page
findings.explanation: Pages are zero based, so the last valid page is `pageCount(total) - 1`. With the current check, Next is enabled on the last page and leads to an empty table.

findings.title: Empty results read "Page 1 of 0"
findings.explanation: When the search has no matches `pageCount(total)` is 0. Clamping the count to at least 1 keeps the label sensible.

findings.title: pageCount drops the last partial page
findings.explanation: `Math.floor(45 / 20)` is 2, but 45 items need 3 pages, so the last 5 people can never be shown. Use `Math.ceil`.

findings.title: No tests for the new pagination helpers
findings.explanation: `pageCount` and `pageRange` are pure functions and easy to test, and the off by one above would have been caught by a single case. Cover 0 items, an exact multiple of the page size, and a partial last page.
